from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the 'Combined' Machine", [
            "Can we combine two transformations into one?",
            "Yes, C represents the single combined transformation.",
            "So, matrix multiplication AB results in matrix C.",
            "Think of this as a dual-lens filter.",
            "The two steps become one single operation."
        ])
        
        # Define visual elements
        m1 = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        m2 = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.3)
        label1 = Text("M1", font_size=24)
        label2 = Text("M2", font_size=24)
        m1_group = VGroup(m1, label1)
        m2_group = VGroup(m2, label2)
        
        m3 = Rectangle(width=3.2, height=1.5, color=WHITE).set_fill(PURPLE, opacity=0.3)
        label3 = Text("M3 (Combined)", font_size=24)
        m3_group = VGroup(m3, label3)

        data = Circle(radius=0.3, color=YELLOW).set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(m1_group), FadeIn(m2_group))
        self.place_at_grid(m1_group, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(m2_group, 'B5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(data))
        data.move_to(self.grid['B2'])
        self.play(data.animate.move_to(self.grid['B5']))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFCC00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        output = Star(n=5, color=TEAL).scale(0.3).set_fill(TEAL, opacity=0.8)
        self.play(data.animate.move_to(self.grid['E4']), FadeIn(output))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFCC")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(m1_group), FadeOut(m2_group), FadeOut(data), FadeOut(output))
        self.play(FadeIn(m3_group))
        self.place_at_grid(m3_group, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Why do we multiply rows by columns?", "The product columns track the basis vectors.", "They show where i and j land."]
        self.setup_layout("The Calculation Rule", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        # A * B * x = y
        matrix_a = MathTex(r"A = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}").set_color(WHITE)
        matrix_b = MathTex(r"B = \begin{bmatrix} e & f \\ g & h \end{bmatrix}").set_color(WHITE)
        vec_x = MathTex(r"\vec{x} = \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}").set_color(WHITE)
        eqn = MathTex(r"A \cdot (B \cdot \vec{x}) = \vec{y}").set_color(WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(eqn, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(eqn))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFCC00"))
        # Highlight B * x part
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(eqn[0][2:7], color="#FFCC00", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(rect))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFCC"))
        # Highlight A * (B * x) part
        rect2 = SurroundingRectangle(eqn[0][0:9], color="#00FFCC", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Why Order Matters", ["Does the order of operations matter?", "Yes, matrix AB often differs from BA.", "Order of transformation is crucial in geometry."])
        
        matrix_a = MathTex("A", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        matrix_b = MathTex("B", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        
        ab_prod = MathTex("A \\cdot B", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        ba_prod = MathTex("B \\cdot A", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(ab_prod, "B2")
        self.play(Write(ab_prod))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFCC00"))
        self.place_at_grid(ba_prod, "D2")
        self.play(Write(ba_prod))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF66FF"))
        diff_pulse = VGroup(ab_prod, ba_prod)
        self.play(diff_pulse.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(diff_pulse.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Vector Space Stage (1 Minute)
sections.content: Briefly define a linear transformation T(v) = Av as a 'mapping' that moves a vector from one space to another. Visualize this as a transformation of a 2D grid: space stretches, rotates, or shears.
sections.example: Visualize a cartoon character, 'Dot', sitting at coordinates (1,0). A matrix A acts as a magic 'stretching' machine.

sections.title: The Concept of Composition (1 Minute)
sections.content: Introduce the idea of sequential operations: first apply transformation B, then apply transformation A to the result. We write this as A(B(v)).
sections.example: Dot first gets 'rotated' by matrix B (a 90-degree turn), then the result gets 'scaled' by matrix A (doubling in size).

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Combined' Machine (1.5 Minutes)
sections.content: Explain that if A(B(v)) can be represented as a single new matrix C, then C = AB. This is the core insight: Matrix multiplication IS the process of collapsing two geometric steps into one single step.
sections.example: Show a dual-lens camera filter: Lens B distorts the image, then Lens A applies a color shift. The 'combined' lens C produces the exact same image in one go.

sections.title: The Calculation Rule (1 Minute)
sections.content: Demonstrate why we multiply rows by columns: the columns of the resulting matrix C represent where the original basis vectors (i and j) end up after the two-step journey.
sections.example: Trace the path of 'Dot' (1,0) through the two matrices. Calculate the final landing spot to reveal the first column of the product matrix.

sections.title: Conclusion: Why Order Matters (0.5 Minutes)
sections.content: Highlight that AB ≠ BA. In geometric terms, rotating then scaling is not the same as scaling then rotating. End with a summary of matrix multiplication as the 'language of composed movement'.
sections.example: Use a character wearing a hat: 'Putting on a hat then a mask' vs 'Putting on a mask then a hat'—the final visual result is drastically different.
